c1.note: Multiple sources (Revenue Memo, Wikipedia, Crunchbase, Nasdaq Private Market) confirm NewsBreak is private and never IPO'd; variant labels A, B, E, F all hold.

c3.note: Company's own release says News Break is a business name of Particle Media, Inc., a Delaware Corporation, founded in 2015 by Jeff Zheng; Wikipedia and NewsGuard response confirm trade name/DBA.

c4.note: Primary press release states Particle Media, Inc. is a Delaware Corporation.

c5.note: Revenue Memo states NewsBreak is owned by founders, employees and investors through Particle Media; consistent with a private venture-backed company.

c6.note: Ownership is spread among founders, employees and multiple investors, and it is private with no public parent; no source shows a single owner.

c7.note: Source says the ownership split has never been disclosed in detail and exact stakes are not public.

c8.note: Source says the cap table is not public and Zheng's stake has not been disclosed.

c9.note: Francisco Partners says it holds under 10% and the rest of the split is undisclosed, so no controlling holder is identifiable; this is an absence claim.

c10.note: Company release says founded in Silicon Valley in 2015 by Jeff Zheng; Revenue Memo adds co-founder Ren Xuyang.

c11.note: NewsGuard page quotes the General Counsel's April 29, 2024 response stating Particle Media, Inc. (DBA NewsBreak) was founded by Jeff Zheng.

c12.note: Revenue Memo (2026) and Wikipedia list Zheng as founder and CEO.

c13.note: He was a Yahoo executive per Revenue Memo and the NewsGuard response (seven years at Yahoo).

c14.note: Revenue Memo names Ren Xuyang as co-founder and a director per the SEC filing; this is a single secondary source.

c15.note: Revenue Memo says Zheng has a significant but undisclosed ownership stake.

c16.note: Zheng is founder/CEO and holds a significant stake per Revenue Memo; exact percentage undisclosed.

c17.note: Company press release of Jan 7, 2021 confirms $115M Series C led by Francisco Partners.

c19.note: Release says Francisco Partners will gain a seat on the Board.

c21.note: Revenue Memo calls it the largest institutional backer, though FP said its stake is under 10% and exact stakes are undisclosed. Medium confidence.

c22.note: Revenue Memo reports an FP spokesperson said its investment was less than 10% after Reuters' 2024 report; the original Reuters statement was not directly seen, so the date is not directly confirmed.

c23.note: NewsBreak's GC called FP its leading investor on April 29, 2024; Revenue Memo reports FP disputed the primary backer label after Reuters in June 2024.

c25.note: Reuters: primary backers are Francisco Partners and IDG Capital, NewsBreak told Reuters.

c26.note: IDG is an early investor, previously raised money and participated in the Series C.

c27.note: Release says IDG was a prior investor and participated in the round.

c28.note: Release: previously raised more than $36 million from investors including IDG Capital.

c29.note: Release says one of the first new unicorns of 2021; the ~$1B valuation figure comes from secondary sources.

c30.note: Revenue Memo says no new round or valuation since Jan 2021; absence claim, medium confidence.

c31.note: NewsBreak's own release says Harry Shum, ex-Microsoft EVP of AI and Research, joined as Chairman in 2020.

c32.note: The 2021 company release lists Jerry Yang as Advisor; this is dated and the current status is not confirmed.

c33.note: Revenuememo and the Revenuememo funding article report NetEase, ZhenFund and Grand View Capital as earlier investors; the NetEase and ZhenFund roles are supported by Chinese business press as cited there.

c34.note: Sources list offices in New York, Beijing and Shanghai, not Seattle; Mountain View HQ is right but the Seattle office is unsupported.

c35.note: Most sources say Mountain View; some directories list San Francisco (Francisco Partners is in SF), so inconsistency is plausible but weakly evidenced.

c36.note: Crunchbase says more than 40 million users across America; 'a month' is not explicitly stated.

c37.note: Launched as the US version of Yidian Zixun; Reuters confirms Yidian described it as its US version until 2021.

c38.note: Wikipedia and Reuters say Yidian was an early investor and divested in 2019.

c39.note: Reuters quotes Zheng saying Yidian management 'did not understand the U.S. market'.

c40.note: Lawmaker scrutiny since 2024 is documented; the no-censorship finding is stated in Revenuememo ('reporting found no ev...') and is consistent with Reuters.

c41.note: Lawmakers and critics, including Krishnamoorthi, have raised NewsBreak's Chinese origins.

c24.note: The Francisco Partners portfolio page lists News Break as 'Consumer Technology Minority, North America, Current'. The saved page isn't dated, so 'checked Nov 11, 2026' is not confirmed by the page itself.

c42.note: Revenue Memo says reported totals vary by provider, with more than $140M disclosed and some providers citing higher figures. c7.note: NewsBreak (Particle Media, Inc.) is still private, with no IPO or SPAC filing as of 2026. Ownership percentages by shareholder are not public. One 2026 guide says Francisco Partners holds less than 10%, but there is no full breakdown.

c25.note: Reuters (June 5, 2024) quotes NewsBreak saying its primary backers are private equity firms Francisco Partners (San Francisco) and IDG Capital (Beijing).

c26.note: IDG Capital was among the first investors. TechCrunch (2020) names it with ZhenFund and NetEase's Ding Lei, and it was in the 2017 Series B. Reuters calls it Beijing-based.
